operations.description:
Creates a new guest account or retrieves existing guest identified by device fingerprint, establishing an authentication session for unauthenticated visitor access.

This endpoint serves as the entry point for guest users who have not registered but need temporary access to the application. The device fingerprint uniquely identifies the guest's device or browser, allowing the system to maintain session state across requests without requiring email/password credentials.

The operation creates a new todo_app_guests record if the device fingerprint is unrecognized, or returns the existing guest account if the fingerprint has been seen before. A new todo_app_guest_sessions record is always created to track the current session, storing connection metadata including the client IP address, current page URL (href), and referrer URL for security auditing purposes.

The guest account includes timestamps for creation (created_at), last update (updated_at), and optional soft deletion (deleted_at). Sessions have explicit expiration timestamps (expired_at) that determine when the authentication tokens become invalid. Guest sessions typically have shorter lifespans than member sessions due to their temporary nature.

Upon successful guest creation or retrieval, the endpoint returns JWT access and refresh tokens along with session expiration information. The access token is used for authenticated requests during the session, while the refresh token enables session renewal without requiring re-identification. This operation is essential for the guest-to-member transition pathway, as the guest ID can be referenced during registration to link the new member account to previous guest activity.

Renews an existing guest authentication session by validating the refresh token and issuing new access and refresh tokens with extended expiration.

This endpoint enables guest users to maintain their session beyond the initial expiration time without requiring re-identification. The refresh token proves the guest previously authenticated successfully and is authorized to continue the session.

The operation validates the provided refresh token against the todo_app_guest_sessions table, ensuring the session exists, has not expired, and belongs to an active guest account. The guest account is checked to ensure deleted_at is null, confirming the account has not been soft deleted.

Session validation includes verifying the expired_at timestamp is in the future, the session belongs to the guest identified in the refresh token, and the guest account referenced by todo_app_guest_id exists and is active. If any validation fails, the refresh request is rejected and the guest must re-identify via the join endpoint.

Upon successful validation, a new session record is created with fresh expiration timestamps, and new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated. The access token grants continued access to guest-authorized endpoints, while the new refresh token enables future session renewals. This token rotation pattern enhances security by limiting the window of opportunity for token misuse.

The refreshed session maintains the same connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) from the original session creation, though these could be updated if needed for security auditing. The guest's device fingerprint remains unchanged, preserving the identity linkage for potential guest-to-member transition.

operations.description:
Restore a soft-deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list by clearing the `deleted_at` timestamp on the `todo_app_todos` table.

This operation reverses the soft delete process by setting the `todo_app_todos.deleted_at` field to NULL, making the todo visible again in the normal todo list view. The todo retains all its original data including `title`, `description`, `start_date`, `due_date`, `completed` status, and all associated `todo_app_todo_histories` entries. The `updated_at` field is refreshed to reflect the restore timestamp.

Only the todo owner can restore their own deleted todos. The system verifies ownership by checking the `todo_app_todos.member_id` field against the authenticated user's session. Attempting to restore a todo that doesn't belong to the current user will be rejected with a 404 error.

This operation is idempotent - restoring an already active todo (where `deleted_at` is NULL) will succeed but have no effect on the record. However, attempting to restore a permanently deleted todo will fail as the record no longer exists in the database.

The restore operation preserves the complete edit history associated with the todo. All `todo_app_todo_histories` entries remain intact and accessible after restoration, maintaining the full audit trail of modifications.

**Related Operations**:
- `DELETE /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}` - Soft delete a todo (moves to trash)
- `PATCH /todoApp/member/todos/trash` - List deleted todos in trash
- `DELETE /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}/permanent` - Permanently delete a todo from trash

This operation performs irreversible permanent deletion of a soft-deleted todo. When executed, the system removes the todo record from the database and automatically cascades the deletion to all associated edit history entries in the todo_app_todo_histories table. The operation validates that the requesting member owns the todo before proceeding. Cross-user permanent deletion attempts are rejected to maintain data privacy and isolation boundaries. ITodoAppTodo.description:
Complete todo entity representing a task item owned by a member.

This schema represents the full todo record returned by read operations. The todo contains a required title, optional description, optional start and due dates, and a completion status flag. System-managed timestamps track creation, last update, and soft deletion.

The deleted_at field indicates the todo's lifecycle state: null means the todo is active and visible in the normal list, while a timestamp value means the todo has been soft-deleted and resides in the trash. Soft-deleted todos can be restored or permanently deleted.

Each todo belongs to exactly one member who owns it. The member relation provides ownership context as a summary reference. All todos are private to their owner with strict data isolation preventing cross-user access.

ITodoAppMember.IJoin.description:
Registration request DTO for creating a new member account in the todo application.

This DTO is submitted when a guest user signs up to become a registered member. The email must be unique across all member accounts and will be validated against existing records. The password is provided in plain text and will be securely hashed by the backend before storage in the password_hash column.

The display name is the user's public profile name shown in todo ownership and profile views. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) capture the registration source for security auditing, abuse prevention, and analytics.

Upon successful registration, the system creates the member account in the todo_app_members table and returns authentication tokens (ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized) for immediate access to member features including todo management.
ITodoAppMember.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Maps to todo_app_members table for member registration: email → email (unique constraint enforced), password → password_hash (bcrypt hash before storage), displayName → display_name. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are captured for audit logging but not stored in members table. Excluded: id (UUID auto-generated by database), created_at/updated_at (set to current timestamp by system), deleted_at (null by default for active accounts), and all relations (sessions, passwordResets, emailVerifications, todos) as they are not user-provided during registration.

ITodoAppTodoHistory.description: Represents a single edit history entry for a todo item, capturing the timestamp when an edit occurred and the new values of any fields that were modified. Each history entry is automatically created by the system whenever a user edits their todo. The entry records only the fields that were actually changed - fields that remained unchanged will have null values. History entries are immutable and cannot be manually created, updated, or deleted. Access is restricted to the todo owner only.
ITodoAppTodoHistory.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todo_histories table. Query by historyId, verify ownership through parent todo's member_id. Return all fields: id, todo (JOIN to todo_app_todos for ISummary), new_title, new_description, new_start_date, new_due_date, created_at. Nullable fields (new_*) are null when that field was not changed in this edit. created_at serves as the edit timestamp. History entries are immutable and read-only.

ITodoAppMemberSession.IRequest.description: Request parameters for querying member sessions with filtering, sorting, and pagination support. ITodoAppMemberSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameters for listing member sessions. Pagination: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100). Backend applies filters to todo_app_member_sessions WHERE clause, orders by sort field, and paginates results. Member ID is obtained from authentication context (JWT), not from request body. Filters are optional - omitting returns all sessions for the authenticated member.
